content:
The number \(17017\) factors as \(7 \times 11 \times 13 \times 17\), so  
\[
17017^{17} = 7^{17} \times 11^{17} \times 13^{17} \times 17^{17}.
\]  
A positive divisor of this number has the form \(7^a \times 11^b \times 13^c \times 17^d\) with \(0 \le a, b, c, d \le 17\). We need divisors congruent to \(5 \pmod{12}\). Since all primes are coprime to \(12\), each divisor is a unit modulo \(12\), with possible residues \(1, 5, 7, 11\).

Compute each prime modulo \(12\):  
- \(7 \equiv 7\), with \(7^2 \equiv 1\), so \(7^a \equiv 1\) if \(a\) is even, \(7\) if odd.  
- \(11 \equiv -1\), so \(11^b \equiv 1\) if \(b\) is even, \(11\) if odd.  
- \(13 \equiv 1\), so \(13^c \equiv 1\).  
- \(17 \equiv 5\), with \(5^2 \equiv 1\), so \(17^d \equiv 1\) if \(d\) is even, \(5\) if odd.

The product modulo \(12\) is \((7^a)(-1)^b(5^d)\). We require this product \(\equiv 5\). By checking all eight parity combinations for \(a, b, d\), we find two cases yield \(5\):  
1. \(a\) even, \(b\) even, \(d\) odd.  
2. \(a\) odd, \(b\) odd, \(d\) even.

For each exponent from \(0\) to \(17\), there are \(9\) even and \(9\) odd choices for \(a, b, d\), and \(18\) choices for \(c\). Thus:  
- Case 1: \(9 \times 9 \times 9 \times 18 = 13122\).  
- Case 2: \(9 \times 9 \times 9 \times 18 = 13122\).

Total \(N = 13122 + 13122 = 26244\). The remainder when \(N\) is divided by \(1000\) is \(244\).

\boxed{244}
